output.summary: Two changes. (1) bloom_filter.cpp: in hashed (non-exact) mode, BFTableFilter::Filter now has a fused path for integer keys (INT8..INT64, UINT8..UINT64) in FLAT or DICTIONARY vectors. A new TemplatedLookupHashed<T> reads data[sel[i]], computes duckdb::Hash<T>(v) and calls LookupOne, all in one loop. This is the same hash TightLoopHash/HashOp uses. A NULL row probes HashOp's NULL_HASH constant, mirrored locally as BF_NULL_HASH, so the result matches the old path exactly. The loop replaces slice + VectorOperations::Hash + Flatten + LookupHashes. Every other type, and constant vectors, keep the old path. (2) physical_hash_join.cpp TrySetExactBloomFilter: a new exact-bitmap tier for range < min(2^27, count*1024). The cap stops at 2^27 once count >= 2^17, so the bitmap is at most 16MB. My first version allowed the tier only when count <= 2^17. That missed q05, whose build has about 455k keys over a range of about 60M, and q05 was +1..+12% (noise). With the tier fixed: full bench showed q05 -13.5%, and a rerun gave q05 -17.9%. In the full run q02 +12%, q16 +5.7% and q19 +7.9% looked slower, but on rerun they were -0.7%, -0.8% and -0.6%, so that was noise. Full-bench geomean was +0.1%; the 5-template rerun geomean was -4.6%. I did not run the warm JSON profile check of q05 lineitem scan CPU that the plan asked for; the only evidence is bench wall time. Correctness: I used temp tables with BIGINT keys and NULLs on both sides, sparse keys over a range of about 2e11 (stays hashed), and a dense range of about 1e8 with 200k keys (new exact tier). The plan profile showed the BF on the hashed test. Inner joins with pre-filtered probe rows and IN-subqueries gave the same results as with SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown'.
output.generality: The exact tier helps every hash join with a runtime BF on integer keys where the build key range is below 2^27 (dense or medium-sparse key domains, e.g. filtered dimension or fact builds over surrogate keys). The bitmap then needs no hashing and gives no false positives. Memory is capped at 16MB per filter and 1024 bits per key. The fused probe applies to every BF on integer keys that stays hashed: ranges above the caps, or sparse keys. It does the same work in one pass instead of several. It does not apply to non-integer keys (VARCHAR, HUGEINT, DECIMAL stored as hugeint, floats) or to constant vectors; those keep the old path.
output.notes: The E0025 tier has to be cap = min(2^27, count*1024) for every build size, with the multiplication capped at 2^27, not applied only to builds of at most 2^17 keys. q05's build is about 455k keys. The fused hashed probe on its own showed no measurable visible gain: once the exact tiers apply, no visible BF stays hashed. Its value is for hidden templates with wide integer key ranges, and I did not A/B it in isolation. The bench is noisy at ±8-12% on single runs (q02/q16/q19 flipped sign on rerun). If you want more, the next step is a micro A/B of the fused probe on a wide-range join.
